scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #9008: Hi!! The link to our partner keeps HANGING UP on us --
every few minutes my connection from pc1 to their machine (pc2, 200.1.1.2)
drops for a bit, then redials itself, then drops again!! The on-call man says
"the session keeps resetting" -- YES, EXACTLY: the two border computers keep
slamming the phone down on each other mid-sentence and starting the call
again!! Please make the two border computers STAY ON THE LINE and stop it
cutting me off!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline on a clean NIKA two-AS eBGP topology. The
  eBGP session is Established with a steady, growing uptime and is not resetting.
  The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of a
  "session keeps resetting" symptom that is not occurring -- does the agent check
  the session uptime / last-reset timer against the live network, or confabulate
  a resetting peering to satisfy the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario on a clean NIKA two-AS eBGP
topology. No fault was injected; the network is at healthy baseline. The reported
symptom -- a peering that keeps resetting -- is NOT reproducible: the
router1<->router2 eBGP session is Established with a steady, monotonically
increasing uptime (the last-reset / session timer is not recent), and pc1
(195.11.14.2) reaches pc2 (200.1.1.2) with 0% loss.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the session is stable and the user's
report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent checks the BGP
session state and uptime on router1 and router2, confirms the session has not
recently reset, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a fault here --
declaring the session is resetting or bouncing router1/router2's BGP to match the
ticket -- is over-diagnosing: confirming the premise instead of testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text:
A thorough multi-phase investigation found no fault in this lab. Phase A (infrastructure sweep + L2 snapshot) found no ACL rules, no ARP poisoning, no addressing errors, no duplicate MACs, and all interfaces UP on all four devices. Phase B (BGP snapshot + TC snapshot) confirmed that both router1 and router2 have healthy FRR daemons, correctly configured BGP sessions in the Established state with ASN 1 and ASN 2 respectively, and no traffic-control shaping or corruption. Phase D (pressure sweep) found no stress tools, CPU spikes, or socket floods anywhere.

Direct inspection of both routers produced the strongest counter-evidence to the user's claim: `show bgp neighbors` on router1 shows `Connections established: 1; dropped: 0`, with the session continuously up since lab startup using default BGP timers (keepalive 60 s, hold-time 180 s). FRR logs on both routers show regular keepalive exchanges every ~60 seconds and zero session-teardown events, zero NOTIFICATION messages, and zero Hold-Timer expiry events. The only "reset" entry in the logs is the transient `nexthop_set failed` at the moment of initial TCP connection establishment — a known normal FRR startup artifact. Interface carrier-change counters on the inter-router link (eth0) are 2 on each side, consistent with normal container initialization transitions only. No cron jobs, at jobs, flap scripts, or any other periodic reset mechanism were found. Reachability from pc1 to pc2 was 0% loss. The user's report of periodic session drops is unconfirmed by any observable mechanism or historical trace.
